newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures end week with a whimper.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures end week with a whimper.

text.p: Rubber futures finished the week with a whimper on Friday in extremely thin trade as market players retreated to the sidelines due to weak consumer demand, dealers said.
"The market was flat and the close was not inspiring because the volumes traded were so meagre. We just wanted to go home after today," a trader for a foreign brokerage house said.

"The market was extremely thin today. We had better volume yesterday and last Tuesday, especially for RSS3 rubber," another dealer said, refering to the more than 14,000 tonnes of RSS3 rubber traded on both days.

Dealers who were hoping for more activity in the afternoon session were dissapointed. Only 400 tonnes of RSS3 rubber were traded and 150 tonnes of RSS1 rubber. No trades were reported for TSR20 rubber.

At around 0945 GMT, May RSS3 was seen steady at 122.75 U.S. cents a kg. April RSS1 was indicated unchanged at 173.00 Singapore cents (US$1.21) a kg. July/September RSS1 was seen steady at 177.50 Singapore cents (US$1.24) a kg.
April TSR20 was indicated also unchanged at 169.50 Singapore cents (US$1.18) a kg.
